ODU_033_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìwòrì.historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity (c. 9th–12th Century CE): Codified as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Wèyìn, teaching deep introspection during times of crisis. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́ Period (14th–18th Century CE): Consulted by palace counselors during dynastic transitions to uncover hidden grievances. Transatlantic Survival: Preserved in Cuban and Brazilian Ifá archives as Oyekun Bori, guiding initiates through spiritual cleansing and warding off premature demise.
ODU_033_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìwòrì.etymology_and_philosophy: Formed by pairing Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness, mortality, ancestral boundary) on the right and Ìwòrì (deep spiritual vision, retrospection) on the left of Ọpọ́n Ifá. Dialectically balances dark existential fear with calm inner contemplation, demonstrating that ancestral wisdom dissipates spiritual confusion.
ODU_033_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìwòrì.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed upon Ọpọ́n Ifá in two vertical columns: double strokes (II) on the right for Ọ̀yẹ̀kú and II/I/I/II on the left for Ìwòrì. Utilizes Ewé Ọ̀dúndún and Ewé Tètè in cool spring water to calm feverish delirium.
ODU_033_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìwòrì.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when a family is haunted by unresolved ancestral disputes or recurring nightmares. Prescribes ethical reconciliation among kin and propitiation of ancestral spirits.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú wòrì wò awo, awo wò Ọ̀yẹ̀kú; a kì í fi ojú tẹ́ńbẹ́lú àṣẹ àwọn àgbà. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú gazes into the initiate and the initiate gazes into Ọ̀yẹ̀kú; one must never look with disdain upon the sovereign decree of the ancestral elders: Teaching mutual spiritual reverence between seer and cosmos.)

Bí òru bá kù sẹ́yìn, ojúmọ́ ìmọ̀ a mọ́; a kì í bẹ̀rù òkùnkùn tí a bá ní àbọ̀ Ifá. (Though the night lingers, the dawn of enlightenment inevitably breaks; one harbors no fear of the dark when sheltered by Ifá: Encouraging perseverance through crisis.)
Ìwòrì tẹ ojú ẹjọ́ mọ́lẹ̀; àwọn olùfẹ́ òtítọ́ ní ń rí àlàáfíà Ọlọ́run. (Ìwòrì stamps out the seeds of dispute; lovers of truth are those who inherit divine peace: Prioritizing truthful mediation.)
ODU_033_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìwòrì.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_034_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òdí.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Dí, governing defensive fortresses, sealing boundaries against epidemic contagions, and maternal preservation. Imperial Era: Consulted before town walls and moats were consecrated. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Lucumí patakís as Oyekun Di, celebrated for preventing spiritual invasions.
ODU_034_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òdí.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (mortal vulnerability) with Òdí (rampart, womb, protective barrier). Teaches that mortal dangers can be nullified by constructing impenetrable ethical and spiritual boundaries.
ODU_034_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òdí.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II on the right and I/II/II/I on the left. Involves consecrated black soap enriched with snail fluid (Ìgbín) and Ewé Ètìpọ́nlà to fortify the human aura.
ODU_034_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òdí.social_and_ritual_context: Employed to protect pregnant mothers, ward off sorcery, and seal property against boundary encroachments.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú dí ojú ikú, ó ti ọ̀nà àrùn; ilé tí a fi àṣẹ dí kì í gbọ́ orin ọ̀fọ̀. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú barricades the path of death and shuts the gate against disease; a household sealed with sacred authority hears no mourning dirges: Proclaiming divine immunity from catastrophe.)

Odi tí a mọ pẹ̀lú sùúrù kì í wó; awo tó mọ ìwà rẹ̀ kì í tẹ́. (A rampart erected with patient labor never crumbles; an initiate conscious of his character never stumbles into disgrace: Emphasizing patience in building defenses.)

Ẹni tí ó fẹ́ dí àpò kò gbọ́dọ̀ bínú sí abẹ́rẹ́; pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́ la fi ń rán aṣọ ọlá. (He who seeks to stitch closed the leaking pouch must not quarrel with the needle; it is with steady care that robes of majesty are tailored: Valuing delicate tools and diplomacy.)
ODU_034_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òdí.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_035_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrosùn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Rosùn, governing lineage purification, ancestral camwood consecration, and unveiling subterranean treasures. Imperial Era: Invoked during royal investitures to clear ancestral curses from the royal lineage. Transatlantic Preservation: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Oyekun Koso, an oracle for reversing sudden misfortune.
ODU_035_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrosùn.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness, ancestral transition) and Ìrosùn (scarlet camwood, circulatory vitality, ancestral sleep). Teaches that hereditary darkness is transfigured into honor through ancestral blood veneration and truth.
ODU_035_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrosùn.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and I/I/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Mixed with Osùn (camwood powder) and Ewé Ìyàlódé, utilizing sacrificial sheep or roosters.
ODU_035_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrosùn.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a seeker faces unexplainable family stagnation or hereditary circulatory ailments. Directs initiates to appease paternal forebears.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú rosùn lójú awo, ìbànújẹ́ yipada sí ayọ̀; orí rere kì í gbé inú òkùnkùn pẹ́. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú anoints itself with camwood before the initiate, turning sorrow into radiant joy; good destiny never lingers long in darkness: Announcing imminent relief after grief.)

Ẹ̀jẹ̀ kì í da awo lójú; orísun tí kò gbẹ la ti ń mu omi ọlá. (Lineage blood never deceives the true initiate; it is from an inexhaustible fountain that we drink the water of nobility: Celebrating the enduring power of ancestral bloodlines.)

A kì í fi osùn pa aró run; olúkúlùkù àwọ̀ ló ní ibi tí ó wọ̀. (One does not use red camwood to destroy blue indigo; every distinct color has its rightful station: Teaching diversity and social respect.)
ODU_035_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrosùn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_036_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Wọ́nrín, dealing with unexpected trade windfalls, sudden reversals of fortune, and maritime commerce along coastal lagoons. Imperial Era: Consulted by merchants traversing the Niger trade routes. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Brazilian Candomblé and Cuban Santería as Oyekun Wonrin.
ODU_036_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (dark stagnation) with Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, sudden commerce, scarcity). Teaches that the turbulence of poverty is quelled by unexpected spiritual windfalls when moral integrity is maintained.
ODU_036_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked as II on the right and II/II/I/I on the left on Ìyẹ̀rosùn. Utilizes Ewé Ọ́kìkà, Ewé Ṣaworo-pẹ́pẹ́, and offerings of honey and bananas to appease wind deities.
ODU_036_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.social_and_ritual_context: Divined during economic instability, sudden business loss, or turbulent community unrest. Prescribes generosity and emergency savings.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín gba Ọ̀yẹ̀kú sílẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ ìpọ́njú; afẹ́fẹ́ kì í fẹ́ kí ó gbé àpáta lọ. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín rescues Ọ̀yẹ̀kú from hardship; the fiercest whirlwind never blows so hard as to dislodge an immovable granite rock: Affirming foundational stability against adversity.)
Owó kì í wá láì sí làálàá; awo tó mọ iṣẹ́ ṣe kì í ráhùn ebi. (Wealth never arrives without honest exertion; an initiate master of his craft never laments of starvation: Demanding rigorous industry.)

Bí ìjì bá ń jà, a kì í gun orí igi; sùúrù la fi ń dúró de ìmọ́lẹ̀. (When the tempest rages, one does not climb the canopy of the trees; it is with patience that one awaits the return of daylight: Warning against rash actions during crises.)
ODU_036_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fatunmbi, Awo Fa'lokun (1992). Iwa-Pele: Ifa Quest.

ODU_037_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀bàrà.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Bàrà, celebrated as the chapter of unexpected royal vindication, poetic speech, and overcoming slander. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by royal heralds (Ilari) confronting conspiracies. Diaspora Resilience: Maintained in Lucumí tradition as Oyekun Bara for averting public disgrace.
ODU_037_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀bàrà.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (gloom, mortification) with Ọ̀bàrà (manifestation, royal abundance, eloquence). Teaches that patient truth-telling dismantles false accusations and converts humble poverty into royal dignity.
ODU_037_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀bàrà.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and I/II/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Sacrificial elements include Ewé Ẹ̀lẹ́gẹdẹ (pumpkin leaves), rooster, and white cowrie shells.
ODU_037_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀bàrà.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for leaders whose integrity is attacked by court rumors. Prescribes truthful public discourse, settlement of debts, and inner fortitude.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú bàrà sọ òtítọ́ ọ̀rọ̀; ẹnu awo ni àṣẹ Ọlọ́run ti ń jáde. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú Ọ̀bàrà speaks the unvarnished truth; from the mouth of the initiate the sovereign decree of the Creator flows: Emphasizing the sanctity of prophetic speech.)

Ẹni tí ayé kẹ́gàn ní àná ló ń jẹ ọba lónìí; àìròtẹ́lẹ̀ ni Ifá ń gbé olódodo ga. (He whom the world mocked yesterday is the one crowned as king today; unexpectedly does Ifá exalt the upright: Warning against underestimating the humble.)

A kì í fi irọ́ kọ́ ààfin; òtítọ́ inú nìkan ló lè gbé adé dúró lórí. (One does not erect a royal palace upon falsehood; only inner truthfulness can sustain the crown upon the head: Demanding ethical governance.)
ODU_037_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀bàrà.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_038_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀kànràn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Pèkú (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú Calls Death to Halt), embodying lightning defiance against malevolent hexes. Imperial Era: Consulted during judicial trials by ordeal. Transatlantic Retention: Documented in Cuban Osha-Ifá as Oyekun Foloko Kana.
ODU_038_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀kànràn.etymology_and_philosophy: Combines Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (death) and Ọ̀kànràn (thunder, decisive moral courage). Expresses the dialectical triumph of raw moral courage over intimidation; standing firm against existential bullies neutralizes their power.
ODU_038_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀kànràn.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked as II on the right and II/II/II/I on the left on Ìyẹ̀rosùn. Utilizes Ẹdùn Àrá (meteorite thunderstone), Ewé Ìná, and ram offerings to Ṣàngó.
ODU_038_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀kànràn.social_and_ritual_context: Invoked in intense legal battles, false incarcerations, or sudden violent intimidation. Calls down judicial vindication.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú kànràn, ikú yẹra; àrá kì í kọ lórí olódodo tí kò dẹ́ṣẹ̀. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú Ọ̀kànràn strikes, and death retreats; thunder never strikes down an upright man who has committed no transgression: Assuring divine protection for the blameless.)

Bí a bá ń ja fún ẹ̀tọ́, a kì í bẹ̀rù ariwo ọ̀tá; ọkàn líle la fi ń gbẹ́jọ́ kàlẹ̀. (When fighting for justice, one does not tremble at the clamor of the adversary; it is with stout heart that one presents one's case: Encouraging fearless integrity.)

Àpọ́nlé ni a fi ń wo àgbà; ẹni tó rúbọ Ọ̀kànràn kì í dáràn nílé ẹjọ́. (It is with reverence that one honors elders; he who offers the sacrifice of Ọ̀kànràn never meets ruin in the court of law: Commending humility before ancestral judges.)
ODU_038_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀kànràn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.

ODU_039_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ògúndá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Gúndá, governing the surgeon's scalpel, the blacksmith's forge, and battlefield clearing. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted by warrior guilds before military deployments. Transatlantic Diaspora: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Oyekun Tekunda for surgical protection.
ODU_039_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ògúndá.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (peril of death) and Ògúndá (Ògún's creative cleaving). Teaches that through courageous decisive intervention and technological craft, fatal obstacles are cut down.
ODU_039_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ògúndá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and I/I/I/II on the left. Associated with forged iron implements, Ewé Pèrègún, palm oil, and roasted yam offerings.
ODU_039_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ògúndá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast before surgical operations, hazardous long-distance travel, or large-scale construction projects. Secures Ògún's protection.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ògún yọ Ọ̀yẹ̀kú nínú ewu; irin kì í bẹ̀rù igbó tó kún fún ẹ̀gún. (Ògún extricates Ọ̀yẹ̀kú from imminent danger; forged iron harbors no fear of the briar-choked jungle: Celebrating technological and spiritual breakthroughs.)

Ẹni tí ó mú ọ̀bẹ Ògún kò gbọ́dọ̀ bínú láìnídìí; àṣejù ní ń bí àbùkù. (He who wields the consecrated blade of Ògún must not flare into senseless rage; excess passion only generates disgrace: Restraining power with self-discipline.)

Bí a bá fẹ́ là ọ̀nà ọlá, iṣẹ́ agbára la fi ń bẹ̀rẹ̀; kò sí àṣeyọrí fún ọ̀lẹ. (If we desire to clear the pathway of majesty, strenuous labor is the starting point; there is no victory for the slothful: Exhorting physical diligence.)
ODU_039_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ògúndá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_040_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀sá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Bìsá, governing strategic flight from catastrophe and placating nocturnal astral societies. Imperial Era: Invoked during sudden military invasions to execute orderly evacuations. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Oyekun Sa.
ODU_040_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀sá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (dark menace) with Ọ̀sá (flight, spirit winds, sudden transition). Teaches tactical retreat: withdrawing to regroup preserves life and ensures final victory.
ODU_040_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀sá.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II on the right and II/I/I/I on the left. Involves eggs, honey, Ewé Ọ̀jìjí, and red feather offerings to the primordial Mothers.
ODU_040_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀sá.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when a seeker is encircled by hostile conspiracies or supernatural panic. Recommends quiet withdrawal and maternal appeasement.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú sá fún ibi, ó bọ́ sí àbò àwọn Ìyá; ẹni tí àwọn àgbàlagbà bá tì lẹ́yìn kì í kú. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú fled from evil and found refuge beneath the mantle of the Mothers; he whom the elder matriarchs endorse shall never perish: Commending peace with feminine spiritual forces.)

Ẹyẹ kì í fò kí ó gbàgbé ilẹ̀; bí a bá rìn jìnnà tó, orísun la ó padà sí. (The bird never flies so far as to forget the earth below; however far we roam, to our ancestral origin we must return: Teaching loyalty to one's roots.)

Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń fẹ́, a kì í fi iná sí etí koríko; ìṣọ́ra ni baba àlàáfíà. (When strong winds blow, one does not kindle a flame near dry thatch; caution is the father of enduring peace: Preaching prevention over reaction.)
ODU_040_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀sá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle; Washington, Teresa N. (2005). Our Mothers, Our Powers, Our Texts.

ODU_041_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìká.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Bìká, governing the neutralizing of toxic poisons, coiling vipers, and malevolent sorcery. Imperial Era: Consulted in court when food poisoning of royalty was suspected. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Oyekun Bika.
ODU_041_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìká.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (shadow of transition) with Ìká (restraint, coiling venom). Teaches that the poison of hatred cannot cure hatred; only absolute moral self-mastery neutralizes treachery.
ODU_041_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìká.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and II/I/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with cooling shea butter (Òrí), Ewé Ègé, and white pigeon sacrifice.
ODU_041_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìká.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when someone is surrounded by slanderous backbiters or suspicious domestic poisoning. Prescribes calm discretion and detoxifying herbal washes.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú ká ọwọ́ ibi kúrò lórí awo; ẹni tó fẹ́ gbẹ́ kòtò fún ẹlòmíràn yóò wọ̀ ọ́. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú coils back the hand of evil from the initiate; he who digs a pit for another shall fall into it himself: Enforcing cosmic retribution upon conspirators.)

Ìkà kò mọ̀ pé Ọlọ́run ń wo ilẹ̀; ìwà rere ni àbò tí kò lè wó. (The wicked conspirator forgets that the Creator surveys the earth; righteous character is an indestructible fortress: Warning against deceit.)

A kì í fi ọwọ́ méjèèjì gba ejò sí abíyá; awo tó fojú fò kì í jẹ oró. (One does not fold both arms to nurse a viper into one's bosom; an alert initiate never tastes bitter venom: Demanding strict boundary-setting.)
ODU_041_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìká.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_042_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Bàtúrúpọ̀n, governing infant health, safe delivery, and protecting expectant mothers from mortality. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal pregnancies. Transatlantic Survival: Revered in Cuba as Oyekun Batrupon for pediatric preservation.
ODU_042_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (threat of mortality) and Òtúúrúpọ̀n (carrying on the back, maternal care). Teaches that tender parental nurturing and communal responsibility preserve the human race against extinction.
ODU_042_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II on the right and II/II/I/II on the left. Involves herbal washes (Àgbo Ọmọ) made of Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, snail broth, and baby-carrying wraps.
ODU_042_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for sickly children, women facing difficult childbirth, or institutions bearing heavy civic responsibilities. Strengthens child welfare.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú pọ̀n ọmọ mọ́ra, Ikú kò rí i mú; ọmọ lúwàbí kì í sọnu lábẹ́ ìyá. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú clasps the child tightly to its back, and Death is denied its prize; a noble child never perishes in the embrace of its mother: Celebrating maternal protection over life.)

Ẹrù tí a fi sùúrù gbé kì í pa ni lára; àṣeyọrí ń dúró de ẹni tí kò rẹ̀wẹ̀sì. (A burden shouldered with patience never fractures the spine; victory awaits the spirit that refuses despair: Exhorting resilience.)

A kì í fi ọmọ ọlọ́mọ bọ Òrìṣà; ìdájọ́ òdodo ni ìpìlẹ̀ ayé. (One does not sacrifice another's child to a deity; impartial justice is the cornerstone of the universe: Forbidding the exploitation of the weak.)
ODU_042_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.

ODU_043_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Túá, governing the clearing of dark shadows through spiritual light, covenant oaths, and religious tolerance. Imperial Era: Consulted when establishing diplomatic treaties between neighboring kingdoms. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained as Oyekun Otura in Cuban Ifá.
ODU_043_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (existential shadows) with Òtúá (peace, prayer, release). Teaches that peace is not passive absence of conflict, but active spiritual liberation from fear through sacred covenant.
ODU_043_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and I/II/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with pure honey, white chalk (Ẹfun), and white dove sacrifice.
ODU_043_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, inter-family reconciliations, and prayers for freedom from spiritual torment.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú tú àbùkù dànù, ó fi àlàáfíà wọlé; ẹni tí ó ba bá Ifá rìn kì í rìn nínú òkùnkùn. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú casts off all disgrace and enters the home in peace; he who walks beside Ifá never wanders in the dark: Exalting spiritual light.)

Àlà tí a fi wọ awo kì í dọ̀tí; ìwà mímọ́ ni ẹ̀ṣọ́ ọkàn. (The pristine white cloth worn by the initiate must never be soiled; pure character is the jewel of the soul: Demanding immaculate personal ethics.)

Ọ̀rọ̀ tútù ní ń pa iná ìbínú; a kì í fi ìjà yanjú ọ̀rọ̀ àgbà. (Gentle speech extinguishes the blazing fire of wrath; one does not resolve elder disputes through violence: Promoting diplomatic dialogue.)
ODU_043_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òtúá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_044_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrẹtẹ̀.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Rẹtẹ̀, celebrated for curing persistent skin contagions, leprosy, and humiliating infirmities. Imperial Era: Consulted by herbalist guilds serving isolation wards. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Cuban Osha-Ifá as Oyekun Birete under Babalú Ayé.
ODU_044_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrẹtẹ̀.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (peril of the flesh) with Ìrẹtẹ̀ (humility, earth, physical convalescence). Teaches that physical healing begins when human pride bows before ancestral medicine and natural laws.
ODU_044_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrẹtẹ̀.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II on the right and I/I/II/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Gbégbé, corn flour (Ẹ̀kọ), and offerings to Ọbalúayé.
ODU_044_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrẹtẹ̀.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for sufferers of chronic dermatological afflictions, bone pain, or societal ostracization. Commands absolute hygiene and humility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú rẹtẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀, ó gbé ìlera wá; àrùn kì í kọjá àṣẹ Olódùmarè. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú bowed low in humility and brought forth vibrant health; no infirmity can supersede the mandate of the Almighty: Affirming divine healing over stubborn afflictions.)
Ẹni tí ó tẹríba kì í kọsẹ̀ láé; ìgbéraga ní ń mú ìṣubú wá. (He who bows his head in humility never stumbles into ruin; it is arrogant pride that invites downfall: Praising modest self-restraint.)

Ìwòsàn dé fún ẹni tó mọ̀ àṣà rẹ̀; a kì í ta orísun wa nù láti jẹun. (Healing arrives for him who honors his ancestral tradition; one does not sell off one's roots to buy fleeting bread: Urging cultural faithfulness.)
ODU_044_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ìrẹtẹ̀.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_045_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Ṣẹ́, governing the dissolution of grief through feminine beauty, wealth, and riverine blessings. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal festivals to banish mourning from palaces. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Oyekun She under Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_045_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (sorrow, mourning) and Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (sweetness, victory, feminine grace). Teaches that sorrow is temporary; when approached with sweet offerings and moral beauty, life blossoms anew.
ODU_045_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II on the right and I/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àjẹ́obàlé, river water, brass ornaments, and honey for Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_045_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.social_and_ritual_context: Divined for seekers suffering long periods of sorrow, depression, or reproductive barrenness. Restores joy and fertility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú ṣẹ́gun ọ̀tá, ó rí ayọ̀ Ọ̀ṣun; omi kì í bá oríire jà. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú vanquished the adversary and discovered the sweet joy of Ọ̀ṣun; running water never quarrels with auspicious fortune: Celebrating joyous breakthrough.)

Ẹni tó fi oyin bọ Ifá kì í fẹ́nú kora; adùn ayé ń bọ̀ lẹ́yìn ìpọ́njú. (He who propitiates Ifá with honey shall never taste bitterness; the sweetness of life arrives after the season of toil: Giving comfort during hardship.)

Bí a bá ń wẹ àbùkù dànù, a kì í fi ẹrọ̀fọ̀ pa ojú; ìmọ́tótó ni baba ìgbéga. (When washing away dishonor, one does not splash mud upon the face; cleanliness of deed is the father of elevation: Enforcing spotless integrity.)
ODU_045_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.

ODU_046_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òfún.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Fún or Ọ̀yẹ̀kú-Bàfún, the supreme mystery where death is swallowed by transcendent light. Imperial Era: Revered by royal elders as the sign of peaceful longevity. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Oyekun Berduni / Oyekun Fun.
ODU_046_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òfún.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness) with Òfún (divine white creation, Ọbàtálá). Encapsulates the profound philosophical truth of resurrection: from the deepest abyss of winter, eternal dawn is born.
ODU_046_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òfún.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II on the right and II/I/II/I on the left. Involves pristine white pigeons, Ẹfun (chalk), Ewé Ọ̀bàtálá, and shea butter.
ODU_046_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òfún.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during grave medical crises where hope seems lost. Reconnects the patient directly to Ọbàtálá's primordial breath of life.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀yẹ̀kú fún funfun gba ayé, Ikú sá fún ìmọ́lẹ̀ Ọbàtálá. (Ọ̀yẹ̀kú shone in immaculate white and reclaimed the world; Death fled before the radiance of Ọbàtálá: Proclaiming the triumph of divine grace over the grave.)

Àlà funfun kì í bẹ̀rù aró; ẹni tí Ọlọ́run bá kọ́ kò lè bàjẹ́. (Pure white linen harbors no fear of the dye vat; he whom the Creator has built up cannot be pulled down: Affirming inviolable spiritual protection.)

Ẹni tí ó ru ẹbọ Òfún ti la ibi kọjá; orí rere ni apata tí kì í yẹ̀. (He who offers the sacrifice of Òfún has transcended all calamity; a well-aligned destiny is an unshakeable shield: Emphasizing spiritual alignment.)
ODU_046_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú_Òfún.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Idowu, E. Bolaji (1962). Olodumare: God in Yoruba Belief.

ODU_047_Ìwòrì_Ogbè.historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Bogbè or Ìwòrì-Gbé, celebrated for illuminating dark mysteries, exposing concealed thefts, and bestowing clear vision. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted by judges before delivering capital sentences. Transatlantic Lineage: Renowned across Cuba and Brazil as Iwori Bogbe.
ODU_047_Ìwòrì_Ogbè.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (deep spiritual sight) on the right with Ogbè (pristine cosmic radiance) on the left. Demonstrates that intuitive perception combined with luminous truth removes all blindness and confusion.
ODU_047_Ìwòrì_Ogbè.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with morning dew water, Ewé Ọ̀yọ́yọ́, and white rooster offerings.
ODU_047_Ìwòrì_Ogbè.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when mystery veils an important civic matter, or when an innocent person is wrongfully suspected of crime. Clears moral ambiguity.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì bogbè tan ìmọ́lẹ̀ sí gbogbo igbó; ohun tí ó pamọ́ kò lè sọnù mọ́. (Ìwòrì Ogbè radiates illumination across the deep forest; that which was hidden can no longer remain concealed: Celebrating the revelation of truth.)

Ojú awo kì í fọ́ sí ojú ọ̀ràn; ìmọ̀ tó jinlẹ̀ ló ń yan ìdájọ́. (The spiritual eye of the initiate is never blinded by confusing circumstances; deep wisdom alone arbitrates justice: Teaching clear judicial vision.)

Bí ìmọ́lẹ̀ bá dé, àwọn alákọ̀kọ̀ a tẹríba; a kì í fi òtítọ́ sọfọ. (When light arrives, the schemers bow their heads; one never mourns while standing upon truth: Exalting the victory of righteousness.)
ODU_047_Ìwòrì_Ogbè.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_048_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìwòrì-Yẹ̀kú, governing deep inquiry into ancestral lineages, uncovering hidden graves, and curing hereditary afflictions. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal burial protocols. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Iwori Yekun.
ODU_048_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (spiritual investigation) with Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (ancestral realm). Teaches that by reverently investigating the deeds of departed ancestors, living generations avoid repeating catastrophic historical errors.
ODU_048_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/I/I/II on the right and II on the left. Involves Ewé Ọ̀dúndún, Ewé Tètè, and black goat offerings at the ancestral tomb.
ODU_048_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when a family suffers from recurring genealogical grief or chronic depression. Restores ancestral harmony.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì yẹ̀kú wo ilẹ̀ tán, ó mọ ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn baba; a kì í rìn láì gbọ́ ohùn orísun. (Ìwòrì Ọ̀yẹ̀kú surveyed the earth and grasped the mysteries of the fathers; one does not journey through life deaf to the voice of one's source: Mandating ancestral consultation.)

Bí a bá rí awo tí kò purọ́, a ó mọ̀ pé Ifá jẹ́ òtítọ́; ikú kì í pa ẹni tó mọ awo. (When one encounters an initiate who does not lie, one knows that Ifá is absolute truth; spiritual death never claims him who masters sacred wisdom: Praising truthfulness in divination.)
Ẹni tí ó ń bọ̀wọ̀ fún àwọn tó ti lọ kì í kùnà nínú ìgbéyàwó ayé. (He who reveres those who have departed never stumbles into ruin in worldly affairs: Linking filial piety to earthly success.)
ODU_048_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_049_Ìwòrì_Òdí.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Dí, governing intellectual fortitude, boundary fortifications against mental instability, and confidentiality. Imperial Era: Consulted by ambassadors before diplomatic negotiations. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Iwori Bodi.
ODU_049_Ìwòrì_Òdí.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (vision) with Òdí (fortress, seal). Teaches that wisdom without discretion is dangerous; the true thinker erects boundaries of confidentiality around sacred projects until completion.
ODU_049_Ìwòrì_Òdí.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and I/II/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Pèrègún, river stone, and goat sacrifice.
ODU_049_Ìwòrì_Òdí.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a seeker's private plans are leaked to rivals, or when someone suffers from racing thoughts and anxiety. Imparts calm boundary control.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì dí àbùkù mọ́lẹ̀, ó kọ́ odi ọgbọ́n; orí t’ó gbọ́n kì í jẹ́ kí ara tẹ́. (Ìwòrì locked away disgrace and erected the fortress of wisdom; a head endowed with discernment never lets the body suffer humiliation: Praising prudent boundaries.)

Odi tí kò ní ẹnu-ọ̀nà kì í gbà àlejò; awo gbọ́dọ̀ kọ́ bí a ṣe ń pa àṣírí mọ́. (A fortress lacking a gate admits no guests; an initiate must learn the sacred art of confidentiality: Teaching spiritual secrecy and discretion.)

A kì í fi orí pa odi kọ́lọ́mọ; pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́ la fi ń gbèjà ara wa. (One does not use one's own head to batter down another's rampart; it is with gentle patience that we defend our rights: Warning against self-destructive conflict.)
ODU_049_Ìwòrì_Òdí.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_050_Ìwòrì_Ìrosùn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Wosùn (Ìwòrì Gazes into the Camwood Mirror), celebrated for revealing future destinies and curing ocular illnesses. Imperial Era: Consulted by royal seers before major dynastic ceremonies. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Iwori Koso.
ODU_050_Ìwòrì_Ìrosùn.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (seeing) with Ìrosùn (camwood, ancestral illumination). Explains that human destiny is written in cosmic colors; looking inward through ancestral contemplation clarifies life goals.
ODU_050_Ìwòrì_Ìrosùn.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/I/I/II on the right and I/I/II/II on the left. Involves scarlet camwood powder, Ewé Osùn, and guinea fowl sacrifice.
ODU_050_Ìwòrì_Ìrosùn.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for young people seeking vocational clarity, or patients struggling with eye infections and optical distortions.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì wosùn wo ẹwà ayé; ẹni tó ríran kì í kọsẹ̀ ní ọ̀sán gangan. (Ìwòrì gazes upon the sacred camwood and beholds the beauty of the world; he who possesses clear vision never stumbles in broad daylight: Celebrating spiritual clarity.)
Osùn kì í pa ojú awo tì; àmì rere la fi ń mọ ọmọ ọba. (Sacred camwood never fails to adorn the initiate; by unmistakable noble signs is the child of royalty recognized: Affirming inherent dignity.)

Ẹni tí ó mọ ìtàn ìdílé rẹ̀ kì í sìnkú bàbá ẹlòmíràn; orísun la fi ń yangàn. (He who knows the history of his lineage never mourns as a stranger at another's grave; it is in one's own heritage that one takes legitimate pride: Emphasizing genealogical grounding.)
ODU_050_Ìwòrì_Ìrosùn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_051_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìwòrì-Wọ́nrín, governing commercial trade, avoiding contractual deception, and navigating price fluctuations. Imperial Era: Consulted by market guilds (Ìyál'óde) in ancient cities. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Iwori Juani.
ODU_051_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (circumspection) with Ọ̀wọ́nrín (sudden shifts, trade vortexes). Teaches that financial volatility must be countered by sharp analytical observation and prudent contract management.
ODU_051_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and II/II/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with cowrie currency, Ewé Ajé, Ewé Ṣaworo-pẹ́pẹ́, and honey offerings.
ODU_051_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when entering significant financial partnerships or confronting unexpected business downturns. Demands rigorous accounting.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì wọ́nrín sọ owó di púpọ̀; ojú tí ó ṣí sílẹ̀ ní ń rí ọ̀nà ajé. (Ìwòrì Ọ̀wọ́nrín multiplies meager wealth into abundance; the open, observant eye is that which discovers the highway of commerce: Praising entrepreneurial alertness.)

Afẹ́fẹ́ Ọ̀wọ́nrín kì í gbé olóye lọ; ẹni tó gbé orí rẹ̀ kalẹ̀ kì í ṣubú. (The gusts of Ọ̀wọ́nrín never carry away the prudent thinker; he who grounds his head in character never falls: Encouraging mindfulness under stress.)

A kì í fi owó ọjà bọ Òrìṣà láìní ìròyìn; ìṣirò pípé ni baba ọrọ̀. (One does not expend market capital upon ritual without accounting; rigorous bookkeeping is the father of enduring wealth: Teaching fiscal responsibility.)
ODU_051_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀wọ́nrín.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fatunmbi, Awo Fa'lokun (1992). Iwa-Pele: Ifa Quest.

ODU_052_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀bàrà.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Bàrà, celebrated for poetic genius, high statecraft, and resolving aristocratic succession disputes. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by royal praise-singers and diplomats. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Iwori Obara.
ODU_052_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀bàrà.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (visionary intellect) with Ọ̀bàrà (manifestation, royal abundance, eloquence). Demonstrates that visionary perception articulated through diplomatic speech elevates leaders to royal councils.
ODU_052_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀bàrà.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/I/I/II on the right and I/II/II/II on the left. Involves Ewé Àkòko, Ewé Ìyeyè, rooster, and kola nut offerings.
ODU_052_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀bàrà.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for orators, statesmen, and scholars seeking career elevation. Inculcates eloquence, gracious manners, and truthfulness.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì bàrà mú ọ̀rọ̀ dọ́gba; ahọ́n rere ni adé tí a fi ń gun orí àléfà. (Ìwòrì Ọ̀bàrà brings balance to speech; an eloquent, truthful tongue is the crown with which one ascends the throne: Celebrating the power of diplomatic rhetoric.)

Ẹni tí ó ní ìmọ̀ nínú kì í ráhùn lójú ọba; ọgbọ́n inú ló ń fa ọlá mọ́ra. (He who possesses inner wisdom never grovels in the presence of the king; internal intellectual depth naturally attracts royal honors: Elevating intellectual competence.)

A kì í fi agídí kọ orin ọlá; ohùn tútù la fi ń gbádùn àwọn àgbà. (One does not chant majestic anthems with harsh aggression; it is with gentle tone that one wins the favor of the elders: Encouraging courteous speech.)
ODU_052_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀bàrà.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_053_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀kànràn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìwòrì-Kànràn, embodying fearless judicial truth, confrontation of corrupt officials, and anti-tyranny resistance. Imperial Era: Consulted when challenging unjust decrees. Diaspora Survival: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Iwori Kana.
ODU_053_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀kànràn.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (contemplative discernment) with Ọ̀kànràn (thunder, moral conviction). Teaches that when conscience discerns corruption, one must boldly speak out; compromise with falsehood poisons the soul.
ODU_053_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀kànràn.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and II/II/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ẹdùn Àrá, Ewé Ètìpọ́nlà, and ram offerings to Ṣàngó.
ODU_053_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀kànràn.social_and_ritual_context: Divined during judicial arbitrations where powerful oppressors intimidate the innocent. Unleashes restorative justice.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì kànràn sọ òtítọ́ láì bẹ̀rù; àrá kì í pa ẹni tí kò hùwà ibi. (Ìwòrì Ọ̀kànràn proclaims the truth without fear; thunder never slays a soul that has committed no wickedness: Championing fearless moral justice.)

Ọ̀rọ̀ tí kò tọ́ kì í wọ awo lẹ́rù; ẹni tó dúró ti òtítọ́ ti kọ́ odi rẹ̀. (Unjust accusations strike no terror into the heart of the initiate; he who stands firmly upon truth has built an unassailable bastion: Affirming clear conscience.)

Bí a bá ń bínú, a kì í fọ́ agbada omi; ìbínú kì í yanjú ọ̀rọ̀ ènìyàn. (Though wrath blazes, one does not smash the water reservoir; uncontrolled rage never resolves human crises: Warning against destructive anger.)
ODU_053_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀kànràn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.

ODU_054_Ìwòrì_Ògúndá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Gúndá, governing engineering ingenuity, metallurgical breakthroughs, and strategic military road-building. Imperial Era: Consulted by royal road builders and guild blacksmiths. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Iwori Ogunda.
ODU_054_Ìwòrì_Ògúndá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (intellectual design) with Ògúndá (technical iron execution). Demonstrates that brilliant thought combined with dedicated craftsmanship produces epochal technological monuments.
ODU_054_Ìwòrì_Ògúndá.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/I/I/II on the right and I/I/I/II on the left. Associated with Ewé Ọ́kìkà, Ewé Pèrègún, roasted yams, and forged iron implements.
ODU_054_Ìwòrì_Ògúndá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for craftsmen, engineers, surgeons, and builders embarking upon ambitious physical constructions.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì gúndá la ọ̀nà ìmọ̀; àdá kì í wọ igbó kí ó padà bọ̀ lọ́wọ́ òfo. (Ìwòrì Ògúndá cleaves the pathway of knowledge; the forged machete never enters the forest and returns empty-handed: Praising productive labor.)

Ẹni tí ó ń wo iwájú kì í gbé àdá rẹ̀ sọnù; ìṣirò la fi ń ṣẹ́gun nínú ogun. (He who keeps his eyes on the horizon never loses his blade; careful calculation is what conquers in warfare: Celebrating strategic planning.)

A kì í fi agbára nìkan gé igi ńlá; ọgbọ́n inú ló ń mú irin bẹ́. (One does not fell a mighty timber by muscular brute force alone; inner craft is what gives the iron its sharp bite: Prioritizing intellect over brute strength.)
ODU_054_Ìwòrì_Ògúndá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_055_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀sá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Bìsá, governing oneiromancy (dream interpretation), calming nocturnal panic, and pacifying feminine astral societies. Imperial Era: Invoked to interpret portentous royal omens. Diaspora Preservation: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Iwori Boshe / Iwori Sa.
ODU_055_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀sá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (clairvoyant eye) with Ọ̀sá (flight, nocturnal spirits). Teaches that disturbing dreams are not reasons for terror, but cosmic warnings that can be converted into protective shields through sacrifice.
ODU_055_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀sá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and II/I/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀jìjí, Ewé Ìyàlódé, eggs, and palm oil offerings to Ìyàmi.
ODU_055_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀sá.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when a seeker is plagued by recurring nightmares, sleep paralysis, or fears of astral attack. Restores peaceful rest.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì sá fún ewu, ó rí ojútùú sí àlá rẹ̀; àwọn Ìyá kì í kọ ẹbọ ọmọ lúwàbí. (Ìwòrì escaped from perils and decoded the enigma of dreams; the cosmic Mothers never reject the sincere offering of the well-born: Assuring astral protection.)

Ẹyẹ orí igi ń wo ilẹ̀; ẹni tí ó ba fojú inú ríran kì í bẹ̀rù òkùnkùn. (The bird in the high treetop surveys the earth below; he who perceives through the inner eye fears no darkness: Praising mystical foresight.)

Bí a bá ń wá àlàáfíà lójú àlá, a gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe rere ní ọ̀sán; àkọsílẹ̀ ọkàn ni àlá. (If we desire peaceful dreams by night, we must practice righteousness by day; dreams are the mirror of the waking soul: Linking psychology to ethics.)
ODU_055_Ìwòrì_Ọ̀sá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle; Washington, Teresa N. (2005). Our Mothers, Our Powers, Our Texts.

ODU_056_Ìwòrì_Ìká.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìwòrì-Bìká, governing the exposure of domestic conspiracies, neutralizing poison, and cultivating unflinching integrity. Imperial Era: Consulted during palace treason inquiries. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Iwori Bika.
ODU_056_Ìwòrì_Ìká.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (penetrating vision) with Ìká (restraint, malice). Teaches that the perceptive mind easily unmasks envious schemers, and that refusing to reciprocate malice neutralizes the adversary's traps.
ODU_056_Ìwòrì_Ìká.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/I/I/II on the right and II/I/II/II on the left. Involves cooling shea butter, white chalk, Ewé Arújẹ, and white pigeon offerings.
ODU_056_Ìwòrì_Ìká.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when someone faces covert jealousy or malicious slander from close colleagues. Commands serenity, silence, and clean hands.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lára rẹ̀; ẹni tí Ifá ń gbé kò ní rí àbùkù láéláé. (Ìwòrì coils back the hand of cruelty from its body; he whom Ifá elevates shall never taste lasting humiliation: Confirming victory over backbiters.)

Ẹni tó ń kọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ ẹ̀bù sí awo ń fi iyọ̀ sínú omi tirẹ̀; ìdájọ́ kì í sùn. (He who heaps insults upon the righteous initiate is pouring salt into his own drinking water; cosmic justice never slumbers: Warning slanders.)

A kì í fi ojú tẹ́ńbẹ́lú àṣírí Ifá; ẹni tí ó pa àmòjútó mọ́ ní ń rí ojútùú. (One does not treat the sacred mysteries of Ifá with disdain; he who maintains moral discretion finds everlasting solutions: Commending integrity and restraint.)
ODU_056_Ìwòrì_Ìká.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_057_Ìwòrì_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìwòrì-Túúrúpọ̀n, governing infant pediatrics, supporting midwives, and lifting heavy collective civic responsibilities. Imperial Era: Consulted by elder matrons of royal nurseries. Diaspora Retention: Preserved in Cuban Ifá as Iwori Trupon.
ODU_057_Ìwòrì_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìwòrì (diagnostic perception) with Òtúúrúpọ̀n (maternal carrying). Teaches that the deepest wisdom is demonstrated in nurturing vulnerable youth and building enduring legacies for future generations.
ODU_057_Ìwòrì_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/I/I/II on the right and II/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ), and snail broth.
ODU_057_Ìwòrì_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for pediatric clinics, midwives, pregnant women, and community leaders undertaking heavy civic responsibilities.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìwòrì pọ̀n ọmọ sí ẹ̀yìn, ó kọ́lé ọlá; ọmọ rere ni àkọsílẹ̀ ayé tí kì í parẹ́. (Ìwòrì carried the child upon its back and erected a house of majesty; a righteous child is an eternal earthly record that never fades: Celebrating family legacy.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í wuwo lójú ìyá rẹ̀; ìfẹ́ inú la fi ń tọ́jú iran tó ń bọ̀. (The weight of a child is never heavy in the eyes of its mother; it is with heartfelt devotion that we nurture the coming generation: Honoring parenting and mentorship.)

A kì í fi ọ̀rọ̀ ọmọdé ṣeré; àwọn tó wà lónìí ni àwọn awo ọ̀la. (One does not toy with the welfare of little children; those who are youngsters today are the master initiates of tomorrow: Enforcing collective child protection.)
ODU_057_Ìwòrì_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
